body:
WHAT
LaTeX in assistant messages — `$…$` and `\(…\)` inline, `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` display — is turned into native MathML DOM nodes by a small parser with no library, no CDN and no extra font. Supported: symbols, sub/superscripts, fractions, roots, big operators with limits, delimiters, \text runs, matrix and cases environments. Anything the parser does not understand is shown as its own source in a <code> element. Prices like `$5, not $7` and `$x$` inside backticks stay plain text.

WHY
A math library would need a CDN or bundled fonts and a relaxed CSP; a crashed or mis-rendered price would corrupt ordinary prose.

WHERE
app/renderer/modules/math.js — MATHML_NS, mel(), MATH_SYMBOLS, BIG_OPERATORS, INTEGRALS, DELIMITERS, MATRIX_ENVIRONMENTS, tokenizeLatex(), makeReader/peek/next/readGroup, parseMatrix(), readGroupAsText(), parseAtom(), parseSequence(), renderMath(latex, display) with its try/catch fallback to <code class="md-math-raw">. app/renderer/modules/markdown.js — findInlineMathEnd(), looksLikeMath(), renderInline() (code spans before math; `$` and `\(` branches), renderMarkdown() display-math block branch after the fence branch.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. renderMath('\\frac{a}{b}', false) returns a <math> element in the MathML namespace containing an <mfrac>, with display attribute 'inline'; with display=true the attribute is 'block'.
2. renderMath('\\begin{cases} x & y \\\\ z & w \\end{cases}', true) yields an <mtable> with two rows and a leading '{' delimiter; \\sum_{i=1}^{n} yields <munderover>.
3. renderMath on an unparseable input (e.g. an unclosed brace '\\frac{a') does not throw and returns a <code class="md-math-raw"> whose textContent is the original source.
4. renderInline on 'it costs $5, not $7' produces no <math> element and the text is unchanged; renderInline on 'see `$x$`' keeps $x$ inside a <code> span.
5. renderInline on 'let $x^2$ be' produces one <math> containing <msup>; a line '$$ E = mc^2 $$' in renderMarkdown produces a block <math> inside .md-math-wrap, and no element is created via innerHTML (textContent only).
